Medpace.why: Phase 1-3 clinical trial services for drug developers: its bookings, backlog and revenue grow as drug programs enter and advance through Phase 1-3 clinical trials, the clinical stage downstream of the chain's discovery and precision-medicine nodes
Medpace.evidence: Medpace Q2 FY2026 call (07-23-2026), CFO Kevin Brady: 'Net new business awards entering backlog in the second quarter increased 28.2% from the prior year to $795.7 million'; CEO August Troendle: 'Phase 1 has increased some relative to Phase 2. Phase 3 has been pretty stable. Phase 1 growth has been driven largely by oncology programs'

players.product: Phase 1-3 clinical trial services (oncology and metabolic programs)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results (CFO Kevin Brady): revenue $707.3 million, up 17.2% year over year; revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026 $1.41 billion, up 21.7%. EBITDA $153.4 million, up 17.6% from $130.5 million, for a 21.7% margin (21.6% a year earlier); year-to-date EBITDA $302.8 million, up 21.5%, with a year-to-date margin of 21.4%, flat as higher reimbursable costs were offset primarily by lower employee-related costs. Net income $121.4 million, up 34.5% from $90.3 million, helped by a lower effective tax rate and higher interest income; diluted EPS $4.25 vs $3.10. Year-to-date net income $245.2 million (up 19.7%) and diluted EPS $8.53 vs $6.79.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $707.3 million (+17.2% YoY); EBITDA $153.4 million (21.7% margin); diluted EPS $4.25

quarterly_data.signal: Bookings and backlog: net new business awards entering backlog rose 28.2% year over year to $795.7 million, a 1.13x net book-to-bill; CEO August Troendle called it a record quarter for net bookings, with cancellations 'well behaved'. Ending backlog at June 30, 2026 was approximately $3 billion, up 4.9% year over year; about $1.96 billion is projected to convert to revenue in the next 12 months, and Q2 backlog conversion was 24.1% of beginning backlog. RFPs were up sequentially and year over year; initial award notifications remained solid but declined sequentially from a very strong Q1. CEO: lower cancellations (down to 'a very good level, not unusually low') were more than half of the driver of net bookings growth from Q1, and cancellations in AIS were also well behaved; pre-backlog is larger than backlog and growing, and has grown faster than backlog over the last year (no figures given).
quarterly_data.figure: net new awards $795.7 million (+28.2% YoY); net book-to-bill 1.13x; backlog approximately $3 billion (+4.9% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Updated full-year 2026 guidance (CFO): total revenue $2.805 billion-$2.885 billion, growth of 10.9%-14.0% over 2025 total revenue of $2.53 billion; EBITDA $618 million-$642 million, growth of 10.8%-15.1% over $557.7 million in 2025; net income $494 million-$514 million; diluted EPS $17.25-$17.95. Assumes a 19%-19.5% effective tax rate, interest income of $21.1 million, no additional share repurchases and FX rates as of June 30, 2026. The CFO models the reimbursable component of direct service costs at 41%-42% of revenue for Q3 and Q4 (pass-throughs ran slightly faster than he anticipated; the year is modeled at the higher end of the pass-through range) and expects some margin expansion in the second half as headcount grows more slowly than revenue. The mix of programs now going into backlog 'might be a little lower in reimbursables', but he said 2027 pass-throughs depend more on which programs earn revenue and their life-cycle stage (later-stage studies carry a higher pass-through mix). More color on 2027 possibly next quarter, 'but certainly in the February call'.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $2.805 billion-$2.885 billion; EBITDA $618 million-$642 million; diluted EPS $17.25-$17.95

quarterly_data.signal: Bookings outlook and demand (CEO August Troendle): 'I would anticipate our gross bookings will ramp up in the second half', translating into a ramp in net bookings assuming cancellations remain in a reasonable range; cancellations are 'completely beyond my ability to predict' and 'always a wildcard'. The market has 'gotten stronger over the last few quarters' and the environment 'remains constructive into July'. RFPs are up substantially year over year and up sequentially by a reasonable amount, with better quality because client funding is broader across more companies; more clients with recent funding are able to move forward and opportunities are moving more smoothly, though he gave no timeline for when funding shows up in awards. He sees no material change in competitive dynamics and no major shift of the programs Medpace chases to China, and said the company is 'making good progress in positioning the business for 2027'.

Customer and therapeutic mix: the top five and top ten customers were roughly 31% and 40% of last-12-months revenue (CFO). CEO: top-five growth has been driven quite a bit by metabolic work, with some large programs among the top five; those very large metabolic programs are reducing and metabolic / cardiometabolic new award notifications have dropped off quite a bit. Oncology was over half of Q2 bookings and award notifications, and he expects oncology to 'retake its position and move up a few percentage points in our mix over the next year or so'. By phase, Phase 1 increased some relative to Phase 2 (driven largely by oncology programs) and Phase 3 was pretty stable.
quarterly_data.figure: top five roughly 31% and top ten roughly 40% of last-12-months revenue; oncology over half of Q2 bookings

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog recognition and conversion (CEO): backlog beyond three years is blocked, and backlog is limited at decision points such as interim analyses - a program planned for five years may carry only one year of backlog until a favorable decision. The higher conversion rate reflects closer attention to gating in the high-cancellation environment (the policy itself did not change), possible differences in burn by therapeutic area, and award size, backlog age and AIS dynamics; metabolic programs are not the overwhelming driver. He expects conversion rates to tend to revert toward historical norms over time but gave no projection of the pace. A decision point can lead to revenue recognition soon after and could meaningfully affect the next quarter's revenue for that program. Most Q2 backlog recognition came from award notifications from the prior year.

Win rate and workforce (CEO): the win rate declined last year relative to prior years; changes implemented primarily late last year and into Q1 are in place, possibly influenced a very strong Q1 win rate, and improvement has been seen. Turnover stayed low through Q2; he expects high single-digit employee growth this year and likely continued growth next year, predominantly in the U.S. and Asia-Pacific, including India, with the biggest growth in the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: high single-digit employee growth expected this year

quarterly_data.signal: Cash and capital (CFO): Q2 cash flow from operating activities $162 million; net days sales outstanding negative 59.6 days. Repurchased approximately 706 thousand shares for $294.7 million in Q2, with $527 million remaining under the share repurchase authorization at June 30, 2026; cash at quarter end $502.7 million.
quarterly_data.figure: operating cash flow $162 million; repurchases $294.7 million; cash $502.7 million
